source_text: μολυνθήσεται.» Μετάσχοι γὰρ ἂν καὶ μάλα ῥᾳδίως τῆς ἑτέρου φαυλότητος, ὁ κολλᾶσθαι μὴ παραιτούμενος. Ἐφίησι δὲ ὁ νόμος τοῖς ἡγιασμένοις, ἐπὶ πατρὶ καὶ μητρὶ, παισί τε καὶ ἀδελφοῖς, καὶ μέντοι καὶ ἀγχισπόροις ἀνεγκλήτως καταμιαίνεσθαι· διὰ τοῦ καὶ ἀψύχοις σώμασιν ἐπιφοιτᾷν, τῇ πρὸς τὴν φύσιν αἰδοῖ, καὶ τῶν εἰς τύπον ἀλογήσας ἀδικημάτων, ὡς ἂν μὴ δοκοῖεν ἄτεγκτοί τινες εἶναι καὶ ἀγέρωχοί τε καὶ ἀσυμπαθεῖς, οἱ Θεῷ γνώριμοι· καί τοι λέγοντος ἐναργῶς τοῦ νόμου· «Τίμα τὸν πατέρα σου καὶ τὴν μητέρα σου, ἵνα εὖ σοι γένηται.» Καὶ καθ' ἕτερον δὴ τρόπον τε καὶ λόγον, ἀπεῖρχθαί φαμεν τοῦ χρῆναι πενθεῖν τοὺς ἡγιασμένους· ζωῆς γὰρ ὄντας ἱερουργοὺς, καὶ εἰς τὴν τοῦ θανάτου λύσιν προσκομίζοντας τὰ ἱερὰ τῷ Θεῷ (θανάτου γὰρ λύσις ὁ Χριστοῦ θάνατος, διά τε προβάτων καὶ μόσχων ἀνατυπούμενος), πῶς ἦν ἀκόλουθον ταῖς ἐπὶ θανάτῳ καταβαρύνεσθαι λύπαις; Οὕτω καὶ ὁ θεσπέσιος Παῦλος, τοῖς εἰς ἐλπίδα ζωῆς καὶ ἀναστάσεως βεβαπτισμένοις εἰς Χριστὸν, ἐπιστέλλει σαφῶς· «Τοῦτο δὲ λέγω, ἵνα μὴ λυπεῖσθε, καθὼς καὶ οἱ λοιποὶ οἱ μὴ ἔχοντες ἐλπίδα. Εἰ γὰρ πιστεύομεν ὅτι Ἰησοῦς ἀπέθανε καὶ ἀνέστη, οὕτω καὶ ὁ Θεὸς τοὺς κοιμηθέντας διὰ τοῦ Ἰησοῦ ἄξει σὺν αὐτῷ, καὶ ἐγερεῖ σὺν ἡμῖν.» Ἐφῆκε μὲν οὖν ὁ νόμος τοῖς ἄγαν ἀγχοῦ τεθνεῶσιν ἐπιφοιτᾷν τοὺς ἡγιασμένους. Ἐπιμετρεῖ δὲ τὸ χρῆμα, καὶ τὸ αὐτοῖς ὅτι μάλιστα πρέπον παραλύειν οὐκ ἐᾷ τῷ περιττῷ καὶ ὑπὲρ τὴν χρείαν, ὡς ἂν μὴ τὸ σεπτὸν τῆς ἱερωσύνης ἀδικοῖτο γέρας. Ἐξίστησι γὰρ τοῦ καθ' ὁμοιότητα τὴν ἑτέρων ψιλοῦσθαι τὰς κεφαλὰς, καὶ ἐφ' ὕβρει προσώπου καταξύρεσθαι γενειάδα· καὶ τὰ μανίας Ἑλληνικῆς ἀνοσιουργήματα, τὰς εἰς σάρκα φημὶ κατατομὰς, οὐδ' ὅσον εἰς νοῦν ἑλεῖν ἐπιτάττει. Συνδιατίθεσθαι μὲν γὰρ τοῖς οἰκείοις εἰς λύπας, τὸ ἀπεικὸς οὐδέν· τό γε μὴν εἰς ἅπαν ἀσχημονεῖν, ἀκαλλὲς ἂν εἴη καὶ ἀπόπληκτον κομιδῇ. «Πάντα γὰρ, φησὶν, εὐσχημόνως καὶ κατὰ τάξιν γινέσθω.» Προτετιμηκότας δὲ τὰ Θεοῦ· καὶ τῶν εἰς γονέας αὐτοὺς, κατὰ τὸν πάλαι νόμον, καὶ αὐτὸς ἡμῖν ὁ Σωτὴρ ἡγεῖσθαι προστέταχεν, οὕτω λέγων· «Ὁ ἀγαπῶν πατέρα ἢ μητέρα ὑπὲρ ἐμὲ, οὐκ ἔστι μου ἄξιος.» {ΠΑΛΛ.} Εὖ ἔφης. {ΚΥΡ.} Ἥκιστα μὲν οὖν ἐπὶ νεκροῖς καταμιαίνεσθαι δεῖν ἐπιτάττει τοὺς ἱερέας. Ἀσύμβατον δὲ καὶ ἀσυμφανὲς τῷ βεβήλῳ, τὸ ἅγιον, καὶ καθ' ἑτέρους ἡμῖν ἀποφαίνων τρόπους, νόμους ἡμῖν ἐτίθει τοὺς ἐπὶ γάμοις, εὐθὺς ἐπιλέγων· «Ἐπὶ παντὸς ἱερέως, γυναῖκα πόρνην καὶ βεβηλωμένην οὐ λήψονται, καὶ γυναῖκα ἐκβεβλημένην ὑπὸ ἀνδρὸς αὐτῆς οὐ λήψονται· ὅτι ἅγιός ἐστι Κυρίῳ τῷ Θεῷ αὐτοῦ, καὶ ἁγιάσεις αὐτόν· τὰ δῶρα Κυρίου τοῦ Θεοῦ ὑμῶν, οὗτος προσφέρει· ἅγιος ἔσται, ὅτι ἅγιος ἐγὼ Κύριος ὁ ἁγιάζων αὐτούς.» Ἡ μὲν οὖν πεπορνευμένη κατὰ τὸ ἀληθὲς καὶ μεμολυσμένη γυνὴ, τὸ ἐπ' αἰσχροῖς ἐπημφιεσμένη ἔγκλημα νοσεῖ, καὶ ἀναμφίλογον
pass_a_gloss: [cont.] will be defiled (μολύνω)' [Sir 13:1]. For the one not declining (παραιτέομαι) to be glued/joined (κολλάομαι) would very easily share (μετέχω) another's baseness (φαυλότης). The law permits (ἐφίημι) the sanctified (ἁγιάζω, pf. ptc.) to be defiled (καταμιαίνομαι) blamelessly (ἀνεγκλήτως) for father and mother, children and brothers, and indeed near kin (ἀγχίσπορος), through going to (ἐπιφοιτάω) even soulless bodies (ἄψυχα σώματα), by reverence (αἰδώς) toward nature (φύσις), and having disregarded (ἀλογέω) the wrongs (ἀδίκημα) [counted] for type (εἰς τύπον), so that those known (γνώριμος) to God might not seem unmoved (ἄτεγκτος), arrogant (ἀγέρωχος) and unsympathetic (ἀσυμπαθής); and indeed (καίτοι) the law saying plainly: 'Honour your father and your mother, that it may be well with you' [Exod 20:12 / Deut 5:16]. And in another manner and reason we say the sanctified are barred (ἀπείργω) from needing to mourn (πενθέω); for being sacred ministers (ἱερουργός) of life, and bringing the sacred things to God for the loosing (λύσις) of death (the loosing of death is Christ's death, prefigured (ἀνατυπόω) through sheep and calves), how was it consistent (ἀκόλουθος) to be weighed down (καταβαρύνω) by griefs (λύπη) over death? So also the divine Paul writes clearly to those baptized into Christ unto hope (ἐλπίς) of life and resurrection (ἀνάστασις): 'This I say, that you may not grieve (λυπέω) as also the rest who have no hope. For if we believe that Jesus died and rose (ἀνίστημι), so also God will bring (ἄγω) with him those who fell asleep (κοιμάομαι) through Jesus, and will raise (ἐγείρω) [them] with us' [1 Thess 4:13-14, adapted]. So the law permitted the sanctified to go to the very near (ἄγαν ἀγχοῦ) dead. But it measures out (ἐπιμετρέω) the matter, and does not allow loosening (παραλύω) what most befits them by the excessive (περιττός) and beyond need, so the revered (σεπτός) honour (γέρας) of the priesthood (ἱερωσύνη) be not wronged. For it removes them (ἐξίστημι) from making bare (ψιλόω) the heads after the likeness of others, and shaving down (καταξυράω) the beard (γενειάς) to the outrage (ὕβρις) of the face; and the unholy deeds (ἀνοσιούργημα) of Hellenic madness (μανία Ἑλληνική), I mean the cuttings (κατατομή) into flesh, it commands not even so much as to take into mind. For to be co-disposed (συνδιατίθεμαι) with one's own (οἰκεῖοι) in griefs is nothing unfitting (ἀπεικός); but to behave indecently (ἀσχημονέω) altogether would be unlovely (ἀκαλλής) and quite stricken/senseless (ἀπόπληκτος). 'Let all things be done decently (εὐσχημόνως) and according to order (τάξις)' [1 Cor 14:40]. And [that] they, having honoured first (προτιμάω) the things of God even above those toward parents, according to the ancient law, the Saviour himself has commanded us [that these] take precedence (ἡγεῖσθαι), saying: 'The one loving (ἀγαπάω) father or mother above me is not worthy (ἄξιος) of me' [Matt 10:37]. PALL.: Well you said. CYR.: Least of all (ἥκιστα) then he commands priests must be defiled over the dead. Showing us in other ways also that the holy is incompatible (ἀσύμβατος) and unmixable (ἀσυμφανής, read ἀσυμφυής?) with the profane (βέβηλος), he set laws for us on marriages (γάμος), adding at once: 'Upon every priest: a woman prostitute (πόρνη) and profaned (βεβηλόω) they shall not take, and a woman cast out (ἐκβάλλω) by her husband they shall not take; for he is holy to the Lord his God, and you will sanctify him; the gifts (δῶρα) of the Lord your God this one offers; he will be holy, for holy am I the Lord who sanctifies them' [Lev 21:7-8 LXX]. The truly prostituted (πορνεύω) and polluted woman, clothed upon (ἐπαμφιέννυμι) with the charge on shameful things, is sick (νοσέω), and has undisputed (ἀναμφίλογος) [cont. s.17: denunciation].
pass_b_english: Cyril: …will be defiled’ (Sirach 13:1). For whoever does not refuse to cling to another would very easily share in his wickedness. Yet the law allows the consecrated to incur defilement without blame for father and mother, for children and brothers, and indeed for close kin, by going even to their lifeless bodies, out of reverence for nature; and in this it overlooks wrongs that are wrongs only as types, so that those who are known to God might not seem hard, haughty and unfeeling; and indeed the law says plainly: ‘Honor your father and your mother, that it may go well with you’ (Exodus 20:12; Deuteronomy 5:16). In another way too, and for another reason, we say the consecrated are barred from mourning. For they are priests of life, and offer the sacred gifts to God for the undoing of death (for the death of Christ, foreshadowed through sheep and calves, is the undoing of death); how then would it be fitting for them to be weighed down with grief over death? So too the inspired Paul writes plainly to those baptized into Christ in the hope of life and resurrection: ‘I say this so that you may not grieve as the rest do who have no hope. For if we believe that Jesus died and rose again, even so God will bring with him those who have fallen asleep through Jesus, and will raise them with us’ (1 Thessalonians 4:13–14). The law, then, allowed the consecrated to go to those of their very closest kin who had died. But it sets a measure on the matter, and does not let them undo what most befits them by going to excess, beyond what is needed, so that the revered dignity of the priesthood may not be wronged. For it keeps them from baring their heads as others do, and from shaving off the beard to the disgrace of the face; and it commands them not even to entertain the thought of the impious acts of pagan frenzy, I mean the gashes cut into the flesh (Leviticus 21:5). For there is nothing unreasonable in sharing the grief of one’s own family; but to lose all decorum would be unseemly and quite senseless. ‘For let all things,’ he says, ‘be done decently and in order’ (1 Corinthians 14:40). And the Savior himself has commanded us as well that the things of God must be honored above even duties to parents, as the old law required of the priests; for he says: ‘Whoever loves father or mother more than me is not worthy of me’ (Matthew 10:37).

Cyril: He commands, then, that the priests be defiled over the dead as little as possible. And showing us in other ways too that the holy cannot be joined or blended with the profane, he laid down for us the laws on marriage, adding at once: ‘As for every priest: they shall not take a wife who is a prostitute or profaned, and they shall not take a woman put away by her husband; for he is holy to the Lord his God, and you shall sanctify him; he offers the gifts of the Lord your God; he shall be holy, for I the Lord who sanctify them am holy’ (Leviticus 21:7–8). choices.why: 'καί τοι' taken as 'and indeed', supporting the concession.
'μανίας Ἑλληνικῆς' rendered 'pagan frenzy' (Cyril's 'Hellenes' = pagans); the reference is to Leviticus 21:5, quoted in s.15, so cited again here.
'Ἥκιστα … καταμιαίνεσθαι' rendered 'as little as possible', since the law has just allowed defilement for near kin ('least of all' would contradict that).

Opens mid-quotation, completing s.15's 'Ὁ ἁπτόμενος πίσσης / μολυνθήσεται' (Sirach 13:1). 'τῶν εἰς τύπον ἀλογήσας ἀδικημάτων' (literally 'having disregarded the wrongs [reckoned] for a type') is rendered 'set aside wrongs that are wrongs only as a type': in these cases the law overlooks the symbolic defilement; the aorist participle is masculine singular and seems to have the law (or lawgiver) as subject. 'καί τοι' taken as 'and indeed', supporting the concession. 'Honor your father and your mother, that it may go well with you' matches both Exodus 20:12 and Deuteronomy 5:16 LXX; both cited. 1 Thessalonians 4:13–14 is quoted freely: 'Τοῦτο δὲ λέγω' replaces Paul's 'We do not want you to be uninformed', and 'καὶ ἐγερεῖ σὺν ἡμῖν' (and will raise them with us) is not in 1 Thessalonians 4:14 (compare 2 Corinthians 4:14); rendered as Cyril has it. 'μανίας Ἑλληνικῆς' rendered 'pagan frenzy' (Cyril's 'Hellenes' = pagans); the reference is to Leviticus 21:5, quoted in s.15, so cited again here. The sentence 'Προτετιμηκότας δὲ τὰ Θεοῦ· καὶ τῶν εἰς γονέας αὐτοὺς … ἡγεῖσθαι προστέταχεν' is grammatically loose (punctuation in the print splits it); taken as: the Savior has commanded that the things of God take precedence over duties to parents, which the old law also required of priests. 'ἀγαπῶν' for Matthew's 'φιλῶν' is Cyril's wording. 'Ἥκιστα … καταμιαίνεσθαι' rendered 'as little as possible', since the law has just allowed defilement for near kin ('least of all' would contradict that). 'ἀσυμφανές' (literally 'not appearing together') may be a misprint for 'ἀσυμφυές' (not growing together); rendered 'cannot be … blended'. Leviticus 21:7–8 follows the LXX; 'Ἐπὶ παντὸς ἱερέως' (as for every priest) is Cyril's lead-in. Section ends mid-sentence; s.17 completes '…condemnation'. Review: 'Προτετιμηκότας … αὐτοὺς … ἡμῖν ὁ Σωτὴρ ἡγεῖσθαι προστέταχεν' is loose; ἡγεῖσθαι taken as 'take precedence', αὐτούς as the priests under the old law, ἡμῖν as the Savior's command to us; English reordered to put the main verb first. The s.17 English opens '…the reproach she carries', which does not join s.16's '…has an undisputed…' (Greek s.17 opens ἔχει τὴν κατάῤῥησιν); s.17 should open '…condemnation.'
